verses.1:1: All wisdom is from the Lord, and is with Him forever.
verses.1:2: Who will count the sand of the seas, and the drops of rain, and the days of eternity?
verses.1:3: Who will trace out the height of heaven, and the breadth of the earth, and the abyss, and wisdom?
verses.1:4: Before all things wisdom was created, and understanding of prudence is from eternity.
verses.1:6: To whom was the root of wisdom revealed? And who knew her subtle designs?
verses.1:8: There is One who is wise, greatly to be feared, seated upon His throne.
verses.1:9: The Lord Himself created her, and saw and counted her, and poured her out upon all His works,
verses.1:10: with all flesh according to His gift, and He supplied her to those who love Him.
verses.1:11: The fear of the Lord is glory and a boast, and gladness and a crown of exultation.
verses.1:12: The fear of the Lord will delight the heart, and will give gladness and joy and length of days.
verses.1:13: For the one who fears the Lord it will be well at the end, and on the day of his death he will find favor.
verses.1:14: The beginning of wisdom is to fear God, and with the faithful she was created together with them in the womb.
verses.1:15: And with people she made her nest as an eternal foundation, and with their seed she will be trusted.
verses.1:16: The fullness of wisdom is to fear the Lord, and she intoxicates them from her fruits.
verses.1:17: She will fill her whole house with desirable things, and the storehouses from her produce.
verses.1:18: The crown of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, causing peace and the health of healing to flourish.
verses.1:19: And He saw and counted her; He rained down insight and knowledge of understanding, and He exalted the glory of those who hold fast to her.
verses.1:20: The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord, and her branches are length of days.
verses.1:22: Unjust anger cannot be justified, for the weight of his anger is a downfall to him.
verses.1:23: For a time a patient person will hold out, and afterward gladness will spring up for him.
verses.1:24: For a time he will hide his words, and the lips of the faithful will recount his understanding.
verses.1:25: In the treasuries of wisdom is a proverb of insight, but godliness is an abomination to a sinner.
verses.1:26: If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and the Lord will supply her to you.
verses.1:27: For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and discipline, and His good pleasure is faithfulness and gentleness.
verses.1:28: Do not disobey the fear of the Lord, and do not approach it with a double heart.
verses.1:29: Do not be a hypocrite in the mouths of people, and be careful with your lips.
verses.1:30: Do not exalt yourself, so that you do not fall and bring dishonor upon your soul; and the Lord will reveal your secrets, and in the midst of the assembly He will cast you down, because you did not approach the fear of the Lord, and your heart is full of deceit.
verses.2:1: Child, if you come forward to serve the Lord God, prepare your soul for testing.
verses.2:2: Direct your heart and be steadfast, and do not be hasty in a time of calamity.
verses.2:3: Cling to Him and do not depart, so that you may be increased at your end.
verses.2:4: Accept whatever is brought upon you, and be patient in the changes of your humiliation.
verses.2:5: For gold is tested in fire, and acceptable people in the furnace of humiliation.
verses.2:6: Trust Him, and He will help you; direct your ways and hope in Him.
verses.2:7: You who fear the Lord, wait for His mercy, and do not turn aside, so that you do not fall.
verses.2:8: You who fear the Lord, trust Him, and your reward will certainly not fail.
verses.2:9: You who fear the Lord, hope for good things, and for gladness of eternity and of mercy.
verses.2:10: Look at the ancient generations and see: who trusted in the Lord and was put to shame? Or who remained in His fear and was forsaken? Or who called upon Him, and He overlooked him?
verses.2:11: For the Lord is compassionate and merciful, and He forgives sins and saves in a time of distress.
verses.2:12: Woe to timid hearts and slack hands, and to a sinner treading on two paths.
verses.2:13: Woe to a slack heart, because it does not trust; therefore it will not be sheltered.
verses.2:14: Woe to you who have lost endurance; and what will you do when the Lord visits?
verses.2:15: Those who fear the Lord will not disobey His words, and those who love Him will keep His ways.
verses.2:16: Those who fear the Lord will seek His good pleasure, and those who love Him will be filled with the law.
verses.2:17: Those who fear the Lord will prepare their hearts, and before Him they will humble their souls.
verses.2:18: We will fall into the hands of the Lord and not into the hands of people; for as His majesty is, so also is His mercy.
verses.3:1: Listen to me, your father, children, and act in this way, so that you may be saved.
verses.3:2: For the Lord glorified a father over children, and confirmed the judgment of a mother over sons.
verses.3:3: The one who honors a father will atone for sins;
verses.3:4: and like one who stores up treasure is the one who glorifies his mother.
verses.3:5: The one who honors a father will be gladdened by children, and like one who stores up treasure is the one who glorifies his mother; and in the day of his prayer he will be heard.
verses.3:6: The one who glorifies a father will live a long life, and the one who listens to the Lord will give rest to his mother,
verses.3:7: and as to masters, he will serve those who brought him forth.
verses.3:8: In deed and word honor your father, so that a blessing from him may come upon you;
verses.3:9: for the blessing of a father establishes the houses of children, but the curse of a mother uproots foundations.
verses.3:10: Do not glorify yourself in the dishonor of your father, for there is no glory for you with respect to dishonor;
verses.3:11: for the glory of a person is from the honor of his father, and a mother in disgrace is a reproach to children.
verses.3:12: Child, help your father in his old age, and do not grieve him in his life;
verses.3:13: and even if he fails in understanding, have forbearance, and do not dishonor him in all your strength.
verses.3:14: For mercy toward a father will not be forgotten, and in place of sins it will be built up for you;
verses.3:15: in the day of your affliction you will be remembered; as fair weather upon frost, so your sins will dissolve.
verses.3:16: Like a blasphemer is the one who forsakes a father, and cursed by the Lord is the one who provokes his mother to anger.
verses.3:17: Child, conduct your works in gentleness, and you will be loved by an acceptable person.
verses.3:18: The greater you are, the more humble yourself, and before the Lord you will find favor;
verses.3:20: because great is the might of the Lord, and He is glorified by the humble.
verses.3:21: Do not seek things too difficult for you, and do not investigate things too strong for you.
verses.3:22: Reflect on the things that have been commanded to you; for you have no need of the hidden things.
verses.3:23: Do not meddle in what is beyond your works; for more than human understanding has been shown to you.
verses.3:24: For their supposition has led many astray, and evil conjecture has caused their minds to slip.
verses.3:26: And the one who loves danger will fall into it; a hard heart will suffer harm in the end, a hard heart will be weighed down in the end.
verses.3:27: A hard heart will be weighed down with troubles, and the sinner will add sin upon sins.
verses.3:28: For the calamity of an arrogant person there is no healing, for a plant of wickedness has taken root in him.
verses.3:29: The heart of an understanding person will reflect on a proverb, and the ear of a listener is the desire of a wise person.
verses.3:30: Water will extinguish a blazing fire, and mercy will atone for sins.
verses.3:31: The one who repays favors is mindful of what comes afterward, and in a time of downfall he will find support.
verses.4:1: Child, do not withhold the livelihood of the poor person, and do not keep needy eyes waiting.
verses.4:2: Do not grieve a hungry soul, and do not provoke a man to anger in his distress.
verses.4:3: Do not further trouble a heart provoked to anger, and do not delay a gift to one in need.
verses.4:4: Do not reject an afflicted suppliant, and do not turn your face away from a poor person.
verses.4:5: From one in need do not turn your eye away, and do not give a person occasion to curse you;
verses.4:6: for when he curses you in the bitterness of his soul, the One who made him will hear his petition.
verses.4:7: Make yourself dear to the assembly, and lower your head to a great man.
verses.4:8: Incline your ear to a poor person, and answer him peaceably in gentleness.
verses.4:9: Rescue one who is wronged from the hand of a wrongdoer, and do not be fainthearted when you judge.
verses.4:10: Be like a father to orphans, and in place of a husband to their mother; and you will be like a son of the Most High, and He will love you more than your mother does.
verses.4:11: Wisdom has exalted sons for herself, and takes hold of those who seek her.
verses.4:12: The one who loves her loves life, and those who rise early for her will be filled with gladness.
verses.4:13: The one who holds fast to her will inherit glory, and wherever he enters, the Lord will bless.
verses.4:14: Those who serve her will minister to the Holy One, and the Lord loves those who love her.
verses.4:15: The one who obeys her will judge nations, and the one who comes near to her will dwell in confidence.
verses.4:16: If you trust, you will inherit her, and his generations will be in possession;
verses.4:17: for she walks with him crookedly at first, and she will bring fear and dread upon him, and she will torment him with her discipline until she trusts his soul; and she will test him with her ordinances;
verses.4:18: and again she will return straight to him and will gladden him, and will reveal to him her hidden things.
verses.4:19: If he goes astray, she will forsake him, and will deliver him into the hands of his downfall.
verses.4:20: Observe the proper time and guard yourself from evil, and do not be ashamed concerning your soul;
verses.4:21: for there is a shame that brings sin, and there is a shame that is glory and favor.
verses.4:22: Do not show partiality against your soul, and do not feel shame to your downfall.
verses.4:23: Do not hold back speech in a time of salvation;
verses.4:24: for in speech wisdom will be known, and discipline in the utterance of the tongue.
verses.4:25: Do not speak against the truth, and feel shame concerning your lack of discipline.
verses.4:26: Do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not force the current of a river.
verses.4:27: And do not spread yourself under a foolish person, and do not show partiality to a ruler.
verses.4:28: Until death contend for the truth, and the Lord God will fight for you.
verses.4:29: Do not be harsh in your tongue, and sluggish and slack in your works.
verses.4:30: Do not be like a lion in your house, and given to wild fancies among your household servants.
verses.4:31: Do not let your hand be stretched out to receive, and drawn back when repaying.
verses.5:1: Do not rely on your wealth, and do not say, "It is sufficient for me."
verses.5:2: Do not follow your soul and your strength, to walk in the desires of your heart.
verses.5:3: And do not say, "Who will have power over me?" for the Lord will surely take vengeance on you.
verses.5:4: Do not say, "I sinned, and what happened to me?" for the Lord is slow to anger.
verses.5:5: Concerning atonement, do not be without fear, so as to add sin upon sins.
verses.5:6: And do not say, "His compassion is great; He will atone for the multitude of my sins," for mercy and wrath are from Him, and His fury will rest upon sinners.
verses.5:7: Do not wait to turn to the Lord, and do not put it off from day to day; for suddenly the wrath of the Lord will go out, and in the time of vengeance you will utterly perish.
verses.5:8: Do not rely on unjust wealth, for you will gain nothing in the day of calamity.
verses.5:9: Do not winnow in every wind, and do not walk on every path; such is the double-tongued sinner.
verses.5:10: Be firmly established in your understanding, and let your word be one.
verses.5:11: Be quick in your listening, and with patience utter an answer.
verses.5:12: If you have understanding, answer your neighbor; but if not, let your hand be over your mouth.
verses.5:13: Glory and dishonor are in speech, and a man's tongue is his downfall.
verses.5:14: Do not be called a whisperer, and do not be entrapped by your tongue; for shame is upon the thief, and harsh condemnation is upon one who is double-tongued.
verses.5:15: In a great matter and in a small, do not act in ignorance,
verses.6:2: and instead of a friend do not become an enemy; for an evil name is shame, and it will inherit reproach; such is the double-tongued sinner. Do not exalt yourself in the counsel of your soul, so that your soul will not be torn apart like a bull.
verses.6:3: You will devour your leaves and destroy your fruits, and you will leave yourself like a dry tree.
verses.6:4: An evil soul will destroy the one who possesses it, and will make him an object of gloating to enemies.
verses.6:5: A sweet throat will multiply its friends, and a well-spoken tongue will multiply courteous greetings.
verses.6:6: Let those who are at peace with you be many, but let your counselors be one out of a thousand.
verses.6:7: If you gain a friend, gain him through testing, and do not quickly trust him.
verses.6:8: For there is a friend in his own time, and he will by no means remain in the day of your distress.
verses.6:9: And there is a friend who turns to enmity, and he will uncover a quarrel to your reproach.
verses.6:10: And there is a friend who is a companion at tables, and he will by no means remain in the day of your distress.
verses.6:11: And in your prosperity he will be like you, and he will speak boldly over your household servants.
verses.6:12: If you are brought low, he will be against you, and he will hide himself from your face.
verses.6:13: Separate yourself from your enemies, and beware of your friends.
verses.6:14: A faithful friend is a strong shelter, and the one who has found him has found a treasure.
verses.6:15: For a faithful friend there is no equivalent, and there is no weight for his excellence.
verses.6:16: A faithful friend is a medicine of life, and those who fear the Lord will find him.
verses.6:17: The one who fears the Lord will direct his friendship rightly, because as he is, so also is his neighbor.
verses.6:18: Child, from your youth choose instruction, and until gray hairs you will find wisdom.
verses.6:19: Like the one who plows and the one who sows, approach her, and wait for her good fruits; for in her work you will toil a little, and quickly you will eat of her produce.
verses.6:20: How exceedingly swift she is to the uninstructed, and one without sense will not remain in her.
verses.6:21: Like a heavy stone of testing she will be upon him, and he will not delay to cast her aside.
verses.6:22: For wisdom is according to her name, and she is not manifest to many.
verses.6:23: Listen, child, and receive my judgment, and do not reject my counsel.
verses.6:24: And put your feet into her fetters, and your neck into her collar.
verses.6:25: Put your shoulder under and carry her, and do not chafe at her bonds.
verses.6:26: With all your soul approach her, and with all your might keep her ways.
verses.6:27: Search her out and seek her, and she will be made known to you; and when you have taken hold of her, do not let her go.
verses.6:28: For in the end you will find her rest, and she will be turned into gladness for you.
verses.6:29: And the fetters will become for you a shelter of strength, and her branches a robe of glory.
verses.6:30: For a golden ornament is upon her, and her bonds are a blue cord.
verses.6:31: You will put her on as a robe of glory, and you will place a crown of exultation upon yourself.
verses.6:32: If you are willing, child, you will be instructed, and if you give your soul, you will be shrewd.
verses.6:33: If you love to listen, you will receive, and if you incline your ear, you will be wise.
verses.6:34: Stand in the company of elders; and who is wise? Cling to him.
verses.6:35: Be willing to listen to every godly discourse, and do not let proverbs of understanding escape you.
verses.6:36: If you see a man of understanding, rise early to go to him, and let your foot wear out the steps of his doors.
verses.6:37: Reflect on the statutes of the Lord, and meditate on His commandments continually; He Himself will establish your heart, and your desire for wisdom will be given to you.
verses.7:1: Do not do evil things, and evil will never overtake you.
verses.7:2: Keep away from what is unjust, and it will turn aside from you.
verses.7:3: Son, do not sow upon furrows of injustice, and you will never reap them sevenfold.
verses.7:4: Do not seek authority from the Lord, nor a seat of honor from a king.
verses.7:5: Do not justify yourself before the Lord, and do not show yourself wise in the presence of a king.
verses.7:6: Do not seek to become a judge, in case you are not strong enough to remove injustices; or else you may be intimidated before a powerful man, and you will place a stumbling block in your uprightness.
verses.7:7: Do not sin against the assembly of a city, and do not bring yourself down in a crowd.
verses.7:8: Do not bind up sin twice, for in the one you will not be guiltless.
verses.7:9: Do not say, "He will look upon the abundance of my gifts, and when I offer to God Most High, He will accept it."
verses.7:10: Do not grow fainthearted in your prayer, and do not neglect to give alms.
verses.7:11: Do not laugh at a man who is in the bitterness of his soul, for there is One who humbles and exalts.
verses.7:12: Do not plow a lie against your brother, nor do the same to a friend.
verses.7:13: Do not wish to tell any lie, for persistence in it is not for good.
verses.7:14: Do not babble in an assembly of elders, and do not repeat a word in your prayer.
verses.7:15: Do not hate laborious work and farming created by the Most High.
verses.7:16: Do not count yourself among the multitude of sinners.
verses.7:17: Humble your soul greatly. Remember that wrath will not delay, for the punishment of an ungodly person is fire and worm.
verses.7:18: Do not exchange a friend for money, nor a true brother for the gold of Souphir.
verses.7:19: Do not forfeit a wise and good wife, for her grace is above gold.
verses.7:20: Do not mistreat a household servant who works in truth, nor a hired worker who gives his soul.
verses.7:21: Let your soul love a good household servant; do not deprive him of freedom.
verses.7:22: Do you have livestock? Look after them, and if they are useful to you, let them remain with you.
verses.7:23: Do you have children? Discipline them, and bend their necks from youth.
verses.7:24: Do you have daughters? Watch over their bodies, and do not make your face cheerful toward them.
verses.7:25: Give a daughter in marriage, and you will have completed a great work, and bestow her on a man of understanding.
verses.7:26: Do you have a wife dear to your soul? Do not cast her out.
verses.7:27: With all your heart honor your father, and do not forget a mother's birth pains.
verses.7:28: Remember that through them you came into being, and what will you repay them as they have done for you?
verses.7:29: With all your soul revere the Lord, and hold His priests in high regard.
verses.7:30: With all your strength love Him who made you, and do not forsake His ministers.
verses.7:31: Fear the Lord and honor a priest, and give him his portion just as has been commanded you from the beginning: the offering for guilt, and the gift of the shoulders, and the sacrifice of sanctification, and the firstfruits.
verses.7:32: And stretch out your hand to a poor person, so that your blessing may be made complete.
verses.7:33: Let the grace of a gift be before every living person, and toward a dead person do not withhold grace.
verses.7:34: Do not stay away from those who weep, and mourn with those who mourn.
verses.7:35: Do not hesitate to visit a sick person, for because of such things you will be loved.
verses.7:36: In all your words remember your end, and you will never sin.
verses.8:1: Do not contend with a powerful man, or else you may fall into his hands.
verses.8:2: Do not quarrel with a rich man, or else he may overbalance your weight; for gold has destroyed many and has turned aside the hearts of kings.
verses.8:3: Do not contend with a talkative man, and do not pile wood upon his fire.
verses.8:4: Do not jest with an undisciplined person, so that your ancestors may not be dishonored.
verses.8:5: Do not reproach a man who is turning away from sin; remember that we are all under penalties.
verses.8:6: Do not dishonor a man in his old age, for some of us are also growing old.
verses.8:7: Do not gloat over a dead person; remember that we all die.
verses.8:8: Do not neglect the discourse of the wise, and be conversant with their proverbs, for from them you will learn discipline and how to serve great men.
verses.8:9: Do not miss the discourse of the aged, for they themselves also learned from their fathers; for from them you will learn understanding and how to give an answer in a time of need.
verses.8:10: Do not kindle the coals of a sinner, or else you may be burned in the fire of his flame.
verses.8:11: Do not rise up before an insolent man, so that he may not lie in wait as an ambush for your mouth.
verses.8:12: Do not lend to a man stronger than you, and if you do lend, be as one who has lost it.
verses.8:13: Do not give surety beyond your means, and if you do give surety, take thought as one who will pay.
verses.8:14: Do not go to court with a judge, for they will judge in his favor according to his honor.
verses.8:15: Do not travel on the road with a reckless man, so that he may not weigh heavily against you; for he himself will act according to his own will, and through his folly you will perish with him.
verses.8:16: Do not start a fight with a hot-tempered man, and do not travel through the wilderness with him; for blood is as nothing in his eyes, and where there is no help, he will strike you down.
verses.8:17: Do not take counsel with a fool, for he will not be able to keep a word secret.
verses.8:18: Before a stranger do not do anything secret, for you do not know what he will bring forth.
verses.8:19: Do not reveal your heart to every person, and do not let him return a favor to you.
verses.9:1: Do not be jealous of the wife of your bosom, and do not teach an evil lesson against yourself.
verses.9:2: Do not give your soul to a woman, so that she may tread upon your strength.
verses.9:3: Do not go to meet a woman who acts as a courtesan, so that you may not fall into her snares.
verses.9:4: Do not keep constant company with a female musician, so that you may not be caught in her schemes.
verses.9:5: Do not look intently at a virgin, so that you may not be caused to stumble by her penalties.
verses.9:6: Do not give your soul to prostitutes, so that you will not lose your inheritance.
verses.9:7: Do not look around in the streets of a city, and do not wander about in its deserted places.
verses.9:8: Turn your eye away from a shapely woman, and do not look intently at beauty belonging to another; by the beauty of a woman many have been led astray, and from this, love is kindled like fire.
verses.9:9: Do not sit at all with a married woman, and do not carouse with her in wine, so that your soul may not turn aside to her and you may not slip in your spirit into destruction.
verses.9:10: Do not forsake an old friend, for a recent one is not equal to him. A new friend is new wine; when it has grown old, you will drink it with gladness.
verses.9:11: Do not envy the glory of a sinner, for you do not know what his overthrow will be.
verses.9:12: Do not take pleasure in the pleasure of the ungodly; remember that all the way to Hades they will by no means be justified.
verses.9:13: Keep far away from a man who has authority to kill, and you will by no means dread the fear of death. And even if you approach, do not commit an offense, so that he will not take away your life. Recognize that you are passing through the midst of snares and walking upon the battlements of cities.
verses.9:14: According to your strength, assess your neighbors, and take counsel with the wise.
verses.9:15: And let your discussion be with people of understanding, and all your discourse in the law of the Most High.
verses.9:16: Let righteous men be your dinner companions, and let your boast be in the fear of the Lord.
verses.9:17: By the hand of artisans a work will be praised, and the leader of a people is wise in his speech.
verses.9:18: A loose-tongued man is dreaded in his city, and the one who is rash in his speech will be hated.
verses.10:1: A wise judge will discipline his people, and the leadership of a person of understanding will be well-ordered.
verses.10:2: As the judge of his people is, so also are his ministers, and as the leader of the city is, so are all who inhabit it.
verses.10:3: An undisciplined king will destroy his people, and a city will be populated through the understanding of rulers.
verses.10:4: In the hand of the Lord is authority over the earth, and He will raise up the suitable one over it at the proper time.
verses.10:5: In the hand of the Lord is the success of a man, and upon the face of a scribe He will place His glory.
verses.10:6: For every wrong, do not hold a grudge against your neighbor, and do nothing in deeds of insolence.
verses.10:7: Arrogance is hateful before the Lord and people, and from both it will commit unjust things.
verses.10:8: A kingdom is transferred from nation to nation because of injustices and acts of insolence and money.
verses.10:9: Why are earth and ashes arrogant? Because in life I cast out his inward parts.
verses.10:10: A long illness—a physician mocks it; and one is a king today, and tomorrow he will die.
verses.10:11: For when a person dies, he will inherit creeping things and wild beasts, worms.
verses.10:12: The beginning of a person's arrogance is departing from the Lord, and his heart has departed from Him who made him.
verses.10:13: For the beginning of arrogance is sin, and the one who holds fast to it will pour forth abomination. Because of this, the Lord made the calamities extraordinary and overthrew them completely.
verses.10:14: The Lord pulled down the thrones of rulers and seated the meek in their place.
verses.10:15: The Lord plucked up the roots of nations and planted the humble in their place.
verses.10:16: The Lord overthrew the lands of nations and destroyed them to the foundations of the earth.
verses.10:17: He withered some of them and destroyed them, and caused their memory to cease from the earth.
verses.10:18: Arrogance was not created for human beings, nor furious anger for those born of women.
verses.10:19: What kind of offspring is honorable? Human offspring. What kind of offspring is honorable? Those who fear the Lord. What kind of offspring is dishonorable? Human offspring. What kind of offspring is dishonorable? Those who transgress commandments.
verses.10:20: In the midst of brothers, their leader is honorable, and those who fear the Lord are honorable in His eyes.
verses.10:22: Rich and distinguished and poor—their boast is the fear of the Lord.
verses.10:23: It is not right to dishonor a poor person of understanding, and it is not fitting to glorify a sinful man.
verses.10:24: A nobleman and a judge and a ruler will be glorified, and not one of them is greater than the one who fears the Lord.
verses.10:25: Free people will serve a wise slave, and a man of knowledge will not grumble.
verses.10:26: Do not pretend to be wise in doing your work, and do not glorify yourself in the time of your distress.
verses.10:27: Better is one who works in all things than one who walks about, or one who glorifies himself and lacks bread.
verses.10:28: Child, in meekness glorify your soul, and give it honor according to its worth.
verses.10:29: Who will justify the one who sins against his own soul? And who will glorify the one who dishonors his own life?
verses.10:30: A poor person is glorified because of his knowledge, and a rich person is glorified because of his wealth.
verses.10:31: Now the one who is glorified in poverty, how much more in wealth? And the one who is without glory in wealth, how much more in poverty?
verses.11:1: The wisdom of a humble person lifts up his head, and will seat him in the midst of nobles.
verses.11:2: Do not praise a man for his beauty, and do not detest a person for his appearance.
verses.11:3: The bee is small among flying creatures, yet its fruit is the chief of sweet things.
verses.11:4: Do not boast in the wearing of garments, and in a day of glory do not exalt yourself; for the works of the Lord are wonderful, and His works are hidden among people.
verses.11:5: Many monarchs have sat on the ground, and the unsuspected one has worn a diadem.
verses.11:6: Many mighty men have been greatly dishonored, and renowned men have been delivered into the hands of companions.
verses.11:7: Before you investigate, do not find fault; understand first, and then rebuke.
verses.11:8: Before you listen, do not answer, and in the midst of words do not interrupt.
verses.11:9: Do not quarrel about a matter of which you have no need, and do not sit in council in the judgment of sinners.
verses.11:10: Child, let your activities not be about many things; if you multiply them, you will not be held guiltless; and if you pursue, you will by no means overtake, and you will by no means escape by fleeing.
verses.11:11: There is one who toils and labors and hurries, and so much the more falls short.
verses.11:12: There is one who is sluggish and in need of help, lacking in strength, and he abounds in poverty; yet the eyes of the Lord looked upon him for good, and He raised him up from his humiliation,
verses.11:13: and He lifted up his head, and many marveled at him.
verses.11:14: Good and bad, life and death, poverty and wealth are from the Lord.
verses.11:17: The gift of the Lord remains with the godly, and His good pleasure will prosper forever.
verses.11:18: There is one who grows rich from his carefulness and stinginess, and this is the portion of his reward:
verses.11:19: When he says, "I have found rest, and now I will eat from my good things," he does not know what time will pass, and he will leave them to others and die.
verses.11:20: Stand firm in your covenant and attend to it, and grow old in your work.
verses.11:21: Do not marvel at the works of a sinner; trust in the Lord and remain in your labor; for it is an easy thing in the eyes of the Lord to make a poor person rich swiftly, suddenly.
verses.11:22: The blessing of the Lord is in the reward of the godly, and in a swift hour He causes His blessing to flourish.
verses.11:23: Do not say, "What is my need, and what good things will be mine from now on?"
verses.11:24: Do not say, "I have enough, and how will I be harmed from now on?"
verses.11:25: In a day of good things there is forgetfulness of bad things, and in a day of bad things one will not remember good things.
verses.11:26: For it is an easy thing before the Lord on the day of death to repay a person according to his ways.
verses.11:27: The affliction of an hour causes forgetfulness of luxury, and at a person's end is the revelation of his works.
verses.11:28: Before death do not call anyone blessed, and a man will be known by his children.
verses.11:29: Do not bring every person into your house, for many are the ambushes of the deceitful.
verses.11:30: A decoy partridge in a basket: so is the heart of the arrogant, and like a spy he watches for a fall.
verses.11:31: For he lies in ambush, turning good things into bad, and on choice things he will place a blemish.
verses.11:32: From a spark of fire, burning coals will be multiplied, and a sinful person lies in ambush for blood.
verses.11:33: Beware of an evildoer, for he devises wicked things, so that he may not give you a blemish forever.
verses.11:34: Lodge a stranger, and he will upset you with troubles and estrange you from your own people.
verses.12:1: If you do good, know to whom you are doing it, and there will be gratitude for your good deeds.
verses.12:2: Do good to a godly person, and you will find a repayment, and if not from him, yet from the Most High.
verses.12:3: There are no good things for the one who persists in evil and for the one who does not freely give charity.
verses.12:4: Give to the godly person, and do not help the sinner.
verses.12:5: Do good to the humble person and do not give to an ungodly person; hold back his bread and do not give it to him, so that he may not overpower you through it; for you will find double evil for all the good things you may do for him.
verses.12:6: For the Most High also hates sinners, and He will repay vengeance to the ungodly.
verses.12:7: Give to the good person, and do not help the sinner.
verses.12:8: A friend will not be vindicated in good times, and an enemy will not be hidden in bad times.
verses.12:9: In a man's good times his enemies are in sorrow, and in his bad times even his friend will separate himself.
verses.12:10: Never trust your enemy; for just as bronze corrodes, so is his wickedness.
verses.12:11: Even if he humbles himself and walks bowed down, keep your soul alert and guard yourself from him; and you will be to him like one who has wiped a mirror clean, and you will know that it has not corroded to the end.
verses.12:12: Do not set him beside yourself, so that he may not overthrow you and stand in your place; do not seat him at your right hand, so that he may not seek your seat, and in the end you will recognize my words, and at my sayings you will be stung with remorse.
verses.12:13: Who will pity a charmer bitten by a snake, and all who approach wild beasts?
verses.12:14: So it is with the one who associates with a sinful man and becomes entangled in his sins.
verses.12:15: For an hour he will remain with you, and if you give way, he will by no means stand firm.
verses.12:16: And with his lips the enemy will speak sweetly, yet in his heart he will plot to overthrow you into a pit; with his eyes the enemy will weep, yet if he finds an opportunity, he will not be satisfied with blood.
verses.12:17: If bad things meet you, you will find him there before you, and as though helping, he will trip up your heel.
verses.12:18: He will shake his head and clap his hands, and whisper many things and change his face.
verses.13:1: The one who touches pitch will be defiled, and the one who associates with an arrogant person will become like him.
verses.13:2: Do not lift a burden beyond you, and do not associate with one stronger and richer than you. What will a clay pot have in common with a cauldron? It will collide, and it itself will be shattered.
verses.13:3: A rich person did wrong, and he himself grew indignant as well; a poor person has been wronged, and he himself will plead as well.
verses.13:4: If you are useful, he will put you to work; and if you fall short, he will abandon you.
verses.13:5: If you have anything, he will live with you and empty you out, and he himself will feel no pain.
verses.13:6: He has had need of you, and he will lead you astray, and he will smile at you and give you hope; he will speak good things to you and say, "What is your need?"
verses.13:7: And he will put you to shame with his meals until he empties you out twice or three times, and in the end he will mock you; after these things he will see you and abandon you, and he will shake his head at you.
verses.13:8: Take care that you are not led astray, and do not be humiliated in your gladness.
verses.13:9: When a ruler invites you, keep drawing back, and so much the more he will invite you.
verses.13:10: Do not rush in, so that you may not be pushed away, and do not stand far off, so that you may not be forgotten.
verses.13:11: Do not presume to speak as an equal with him, and do not trust his many words; for through much talk he will test you, and as if smiling, he will examine you.
verses.13:12: Merciless is the one who does not guard words, and he will by no means hold back from affliction and chains.
verses.13:13: Be on guard and take great care, because you are walking with your downfall.
verses.13:15: Every living creature loves what is like itself, and every person his neighbor.
verses.13:16: All flesh gathers according to kind, and a man will cling to one like himself.
verses.13:17: What will a wolf have in common with a lamb? So is a sinner with a godly person.
verses.13:18: What peace does a hyena have with a dog? And what peace does a rich person have with a needy person?
verses.13:19: Wild donkeys in the wilderness are the prey of lions; so the poor are the pastures of the rich.
verses.13:20: Humility is an abomination to an arrogant person; so a poor person is an abomination to a rich person.
verses.13:21: A rich person who staggers is supported by friends, but a lowly person who falls is even pushed away by friends.
verses.13:22: When a rich person slips, there are many helpers; he spoke things not to be spoken, and they justified him. A lowly person slipped, and they even rebuked him; he uttered understanding, and no place was given to him.
verses.13:23: A rich person spoke, and all kept silent, and they exalted his word to the clouds; a poor person spoke, and they said, "Who is this?" And if he stumbles, they will overthrow him as well.
verses.13:24: Wealth is good in which there is no sin, and poverty is evil in the mouths of a godly person.
verses.13:25: A person's heart changes his face, whether for good or for evil.
verses.13:26: The trace of a heart in good things is a cheerful face, and the discovery of proverbs is thoughts with toil.
verses.14:1: Blessed is the man who has not slipped with his mouth, and has not been pierced by the grief of sin.
verses.14:2: Blessed is the one whom his soul has not condemned, and who has not fallen from his hope.
verses.14:3: Wealth is not fitting for a stingy man, and what is the use of possessions to a grudging person?
verses.14:4: The one who gathers from his own soul gathers for others, and others will live in luxury on his good things.
verses.14:5: The one who is evil to himself, to whom will he be good? And he will by no means rejoice in his possessions.
verses.14:6: There is no one more evil than the one who begrudges himself, and this is the repayment of his wickedness.
verses.14:7: And even if he does good, he does it in forgetfulness, and in the end he reveals his wickedness.
verses.14:8: Evil is the one who begrudges with his eye, turning away his face and overlooking souls.
verses.14:9: The eye of a greedy person is not satisfied with a portion, and evil injustice will dry up a soul.
verses.14:10: An evil eye is envious over bread, and is lacking at his table.
verses.14:11: Child, according to what you have, do good to yourself, and bring offerings to the Lord worthily.
verses.14:12: Remember that death will not delay, and the decree of Hades has not been shown to you.
verses.14:13: Before you die, do good to a friend, and according to your strength reach out and give to him.
verses.14:14: Do not miss out on a good day, and may a portion of a good desire not pass you by.
verses.14:15: Will you not leave your labors to another, and your toils for division by lot?
verses.14:16: Give and receive, and indulge your soul, because it is not possible in Hades to seek luxury.
verses.14:17: All flesh grows old like a garment; for the decree from of old is, "You will surely die."
verses.14:18: Like a flourishing leaf on a thick tree, some it sheds, and others it sprouts; so is a generation of flesh and blood: one dies, and another is born.
verses.14:19: Every decaying work fails, and the one who makes it will depart with it.
verses.14:20: Blessed is the man who will die in wisdom, and who will reason in his understanding.
verses.14:21: The one who considers her ways in his heart will also gain understanding in her secrets.
verses.14:22: Go out after her like a tracker, and lie in wait at her entrances.
verses.14:23: The one who peers through her windows will also listen at her doorways.
verses.14:24: The one who lodges close to her house will also drive a peg into her walls.
verses.14:25: He will pitch his tent beside her, and he will lodge in a lodging place of good things.
verses.14:26: He will place his children in her shelter, and he will camp beneath her branches.
verses.14:27: He will be sheltered by her from heat, and he will lodge in her glory.
verses.15:1: The one who fears the Lord will do this, and the one who holds fast to the law will obtain her.
verses.15:2: And she will meet him like a mother, and like a virgin wife she will welcome him.
verses.15:3: She will feed him bread of understanding, and she will give him water of wisdom to drink.
verses.15:4: He will lean on her and will by no means give way, and he will hold fast to her and will by no means be put to shame.
verses.15:5: And she will exalt him above his neighbors, and in the midst of the assembly she will open his mouth.
verses.15:6: He will inherit gladness and a crown of exultation and an eternal name.
verses.15:7: People without understanding will by no means obtain her, and sinful men will by no means see her.
verses.15:8: She is far from arrogance, and lying men will by no means remember her.
verses.15:9: Praise is not fitting in the mouth of a sinner, because it was not sent from the Lord.
verses.15:10: For praise will be spoken in wisdom, and the Lord will prosper it.
verses.15:11: Do not say, "Because of the Lord I fell away," for what He has hated, you must not do.
verses.15:12: Do not say, "He Himself led me astray," for He has no need of a sinful man.
verses.15:13: The Lord has hated every abomination, and it is not loved by those who fear Him.
verses.15:14: He Himself made man from the beginning, and left him in the hand of his own deliberation.
verses.15:15: If you wish, you will keep commandments, and to practice faithfulness is a matter of choice.
verses.15:16: He has set fire and water before you; to whichever you wish, you will stretch out your hand.
verses.15:17: Before people are life and death, and whatever one chooses will be given to him.
verses.15:18: For great is the wisdom of the Lord; He is mighty in power and sees all things.
verses.15:19: And His eyes are upon those who fear Him, and He Himself will know every deed of a person.
verses.15:20: And He has not commanded anyone to be ungodly, and He has not given anyone permission to sin.
verses.16:1: Do not desire a multitude of useless children, nor rejoice over ungodly sons.
verses.16:2: If they multiply, do not rejoice over them; if the fear of the Lord is not with them,
verses.16:3: do not trust in their life, and do not rely on their place; for one is better than a thousand, and to die childless than to have ungodly children.
verses.16:4: For from one person of understanding a city will be populated, but a tribe of lawless people will be made desolate.
verses.16:5: Many such things I have seen with my eyes, and mightier things than these my ear has heard.
verses.16:6: In an assembly of sinners fire will be kindled, and in a disobedient nation wrath was kindled.
verses.16:7: He did not grant pardon for the ancient giants, who rebelled in their strength;
verses.16:8: He did not spare the community where Lot sojourned, whom He detested because of their arrogance;
verses.16:9: He did not have mercy on a nation of destruction, those who were removed in their sins;
verses.16:10: and likewise six hundred thousand foot soldiers, those who were gathered together in their hardness of heart.
verses.16:11: Even if there is one stiff-necked person, this is a marvel if he will go unpunished. For mercy and wrath are from Him; He is mighty in pardons and pours out wrath.
verses.16:12: According to His great mercy, so also great is His reproof; He will judge a man according to his works.
verses.16:13: A sinner will not escape with plunder, and He will by no means delay the endurance of a godly person.
verses.16:14: He will make a place for every act of mercy; each one will find according to his works.
verses.16:17: Do not say, "I will be hidden from the Lord; will anyone from on high remember me? Among a vast people I will by no means be remembered, for what is my soul in an immeasurable creation?"
verses.16:18: Look, heaven and God's heaven of heaven, the abyss and the earth will be shaken at His visitation;
verses.16:19: together the mountains and the foundations of the earth quake with trembling when He looks upon them.
verses.16:20: And on these things no heart will reflect; and who will ponder His ways?
verses.16:21: And there is a tempest that no one will see, and most of His works are in hidden places.
verses.16:22: Who will declare works of righteousness? Or who will endure? For the covenant is far away.
verses.16:23: One lacking in heart thinks these things, and a senseless and straying man thinks foolish things.
verses.16:24: Listen to me, child, and learn knowledge, and pay attention to my words with your heart.
verses.16:25: I set forth instruction by weight, and with exactness I declare knowledge.
verses.16:26: In the judgment of the Lord are His works from the beginning, and from the making of them He separated their portions.
verses.16:27: He set His works in order forever, and their dominions for their generations; they neither hungered nor grew weary, and they did not cease from their works;
verses.16:28: not one crowded its neighbor, and forever they will not disobey His word.
verses.16:29: And after these things the Lord looked upon the earth and filled it with His good things;
verses.16:30: with the life of every living creature He covered its face, and to it is their return.
verses.17:1: The Lord created man from earth, and again He returned him to it.
verses.17:2: He gave them numbered days and a time, and He gave them authority over the things upon it.
verses.17:3: According to themselves He clothed them with strength, and according to His image He made them;
verses.17:4: and He placed the fear of him upon all flesh, and appointed them to have dominion over wild beasts and birds.
verses.17:6: He gave them deliberation and a tongue and eyes, ears and a heart to think.
verses.17:7: He filled them with knowledge of understanding, and He showed them good and evil.
verses.17:8: He set His eye upon their hearts, to show them the majesty of His works,
verses.17:10: so that they might recount the splendors of His works. And they will praise the name of holiness.
verses.17:11: He added knowledge to them, and He gave them a law of life as an inheritance.
verses.17:12: He established an everlasting covenant with them, and He showed them His judgments.
verses.17:13: Their eyes saw the majesty of glory, and their ear heard the glory of their voice.
verses.17:14: And He said to them, "Beware of every unrighteous thing," and He commanded each of them concerning his neighbor.
verses.17:15: Their ways are before Him continually; they will not be hidden from His eyes.
verses.17:17: For every nation He appointed a ruler, and the Lord's portion is Israel.
verses.17:19: All their works are like the sun before Him, and His eyes are continually upon their ways.
verses.17:20: Their unrighteous deeds were not hidden from Him, and all their sins are before the Lord.
verses.17:22: A man's act of mercy is like a signet ring with Him, and He will guard a person's kindness like the pupil of an eye.
verses.17:23: After these things He will rise up and repay them, and He will render their repayment upon their head.
verses.17:24: Yet to those who repent He gave a return, and He encouraged those failing in endurance.
verses.17:25: Turn back to the Lord and forsake sins; plead before His face and lessen offense.
verses.17:26: Return to the Most High and turn away from unrighteousness, and greatly hate abomination.
verses.17:27: Who will praise the Most High in Hades instead of the living and those who give thanksgiving?
verses.17:28: From one who is dead, as from one who does not even exist, thanksgiving perishes; one who is alive and healthy will praise the Lord.
verses.17:29: How great is the mercy of the Lord, and pardon for those who turn back to Him!
verses.17:30: For not all things can be in human beings, because a son of man is not immortal.
verses.17:31: What is brighter than the sun? Yet even this fails; and an evil person will ponder flesh and blood.
verses.17:32: He Himself inspects the host of the height of heaven, and all human beings are earth and ashes.
verses.18:1: He who lives forever created all things together.
verses.18:2: The Lord alone will be justified.
verses.18:4: He has enabled no one to declare His works, and who will trace out His great deeds?
verses.18:5: Who will count the might of His majesty? And who will go on to recount His mercies?
verses.18:6: It is not possible to diminish or to add, and it is not possible to trace out the wonders of the Lord.
verses.18:7: When a man finishes, then he begins, and when he stops, then he will be perplexed.
verses.18:8: What is man, and what is his usefulness? What is his good, and what is his evil?
verses.18:9: The number of a man's days is at most a hundred years.
verses.18:10: Like a drop of water from the sea and a grain of sand, so are a few years in a day of eternity.
verses.18:11: For this reason the Lord was patient with them, and poured out His mercy upon them.
verses.18:12: He saw and recognized that their ruin was grievous; for this reason He multiplied His atonement.
verses.18:13: The mercy of a man is upon his neighbor, but the mercy of the Lord is upon all flesh; He reproves and disciplines and teaches and brings back, as a shepherd does his flock.
verses.18:14: He has mercy on those who accept discipline and those who hasten to His judgments.
verses.18:15: Child, in good deeds do not bring a blemish, nor in any gift grief of words.
verses.18:16: Will not dew relieve the scorching heat? So a word is better than a gift.
verses.18:17: Look, is not a word above a good gift? And both are with a gracious man.
verses.18:18: A fool will reproach ungraciously, and the gift of a grudging man wastes away the eyes.
verses.18:19: Before speaking, learn, and before sickness, take care of yourself.
verses.18:20: Before judgment, examine yourself, and in the hour of visitation you will find atonement.
verses.18:21: Before you become sick, humble yourself, and in a time of sins, show repentance.
verses.18:22: Do not be hindered from paying a vow in due time, and do not wait until death to be justified.
verses.18:23: Before making a vow, prepare yourself, and do not become like a man testing the Lord.
verses.18:24: Remember wrath in the days of death, and the time of vengeance at the turning away of the face.
verses.18:25: Remember a time of famine in a time of plenty, poverty and need in days of wealth.
verses.18:26: From morning until evening time changes, and all things are swift before the Lord.
verses.18:27: A wise man will be cautious in everything, and in days of sins he will guard against wrongdoing.
verses.18:28: Everyone with understanding has come to know wisdom, and to the one who finds it he will give praise.
verses.18:29: Those with understanding in words have themselves also become wise, and have poured forth precise proverbs.
verses.18:30: Self-control of the soul. Do not go after your desires, and restrain yourself from your appetites.
verses.18:31: If you supply your soul with the pleasure of desire, it will make you an object of gloating to your enemies.
verses.18:32: Do not delight in great luxury; do not be bound to its expense.
verses.18:33: Do not become poor by feasting on borrowed money, when you have nothing in your purse.
verses.19:1: A drunken laborer will not become rich; the one who despises small things will fall little by little.
verses.19:2: Wine and women will lead astray those with understanding, and the one who clings to prostitutes will be more reckless.
verses.19:3: Decay and worms will inherit him, and a reckless soul will be taken away.
verses.19:4: The one who trusts quickly is flighty in heart, and the one who sins will wrong his own soul.
verses.19:5: The one who delights in heart will be condemned,
verses.19:6: and the one who hates chatter has less evil.
verses.19:7: Never repeat a word, and nothing at all will be diminished for you.
verses.19:8: To friend and enemy do not tell it, and unless it is a sin for you, do not reveal it.
verses.19:9: For he has heard you and guarded himself against you, and in time he will hate you.
verses.19:10: Have you heard a word? Let it die with you. Take courage, it will certainly not burst you.
verses.19:11: Because of a word a fool will suffer labor pains, as a woman giving birth does because of a baby.
verses.19:12: An arrow lodged in a thigh of flesh; so is a word in the belly of a fool.
verses.19:13: Reprove a friend; perhaps he did not do it, and if he did anything, so that he will not do it again.
verses.19:14: Reprove your friend; perhaps he did not say it, and if he has said it, so that he will not repeat it.
verses.19:15: Reprove a friend, for slander often occurs, and do not believe every word.
verses.19:16: There is one who slips, and not from the soul; and who has not sinned with his tongue?
verses.19:17: Reprove your neighbor before threatening, and give place to the law of the Most High.
verses.19:20: All wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and in all wisdom is the doing of the law.
verses.19:22: And the knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom, and nowhere is the counsel of sinners prudence.
verses.19:23: There is wickedness, and it is an abomination, and there is a foolish person lacking in wisdom.
verses.19:24: Better is a reverent person who falls short in understanding than one who abounds in prudence and transgresses the law.
verses.19:25: There is a precise cleverness, and it is unjust, and there is one who perverts favor to bring forth a judgment.
verses.19:26: There is one who acts wickedly, bowed down in gloom, and what is within him is full of deceit.
verses.19:27: Bowing down his face and pretending to be deaf, where he has not been recognized he will take you by surprise.
verses.19:28: And if by a lack of strength he is prevented from sinning, if he finds an opportunity, he will do evil.
verses.19:29: From appearance a man will be recognized, and from the meeting of the face a perceptive person will be recognized.
verses.19:30: The attire of a man and the laughter of the teeth and the steps of a person declare the things concerning him.
verses.20:1: There is a reproof that is not timely, and there is one who keeps silent, and he is prudent.
verses.20:2: How good it is to reprove rather than to be angry,
verses.20:3: and the one who confesses will be kept from loss.
verses.20:4: A eunuch's desire to deflower a young woman—so is the one who executes judgments by violence.
verses.20:5: There is one who keeps silent and is found wise, and there is one who is hated because of much talk.
verses.20:6: There is one who keeps silent, for he has no answer, and there is one who keeps silent, knowing the right time.
verses.20:7: A wise person will remain silent until the right time, but the braggart and senseless one will overstep the right time.
verses.20:8: The one who is excessive in speech will be detested, and the one who assumes authority for himself will be hated.
verses.20:9: There is success in misfortunes for a man, and there is a find that leads to loss.
verses.20:10: There is a gift that will not profit you, and there is a gift whose repayment is double.
verses.20:11: There is loss on account of glory, and there is one who has lifted his head from humiliation.
verses.20:12: There is one who buys many things for little and pays for them sevenfold.
verses.20:13: The wise person will make himself endearing in speech, but the favors of fools will be poured out.
verses.20:14: The gift of a senseless person will not profit you, for his eyes are many instead of one.
verses.20:15: He will give little and reproach much, and he will open his mouth like a herald; today he will lend and tomorrow he will demand it back—such a person is hateful.
verses.20:16: A fool will say, "I have no friend, and there is no gratitude for my good deeds; those who eat my bread are wicked in tongue."
verses.20:17: How often and how many will laugh at him?
verses.20:18: A slip on the floor rather than with the tongue; so the fall of the wicked will come swiftly.
verses.20:19: An ungracious person is an untimely tale; it will be continually in the mouth of the undisciplined.
verses.20:20: From the mouth of a fool a proverb will be rejected, for he will by no means speak it at its right time.
verses.20:21: There is one who is kept from sinning by poverty, and in his rest he will not be stung with remorse.
verses.20:22: There is one who destroys his soul through shame, and because of a senseless person he will destroy it.
verses.20:23: There is one who makes a promise to a friend out of shame, and has gained him as an enemy for nothing.
verses.20:24: A lie is an evil blemish in a person; it will be continually in the mouth of the undisciplined.
verses.20:25: A thief is preferable to one who continually persists in lying, yet both will inherit destruction.
verses.20:26: The character of a lying person is dishonor, and his shame is with him continually.
verses.20:27: Words of proverbs. The wise person will advance himself in words, and a prudent person will please the great.
verses.20:28: The one who works the land will raise high his heap of grain, and the one who pleases the great will atone for wrongdoing.
verses.20:29: Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise, and like a muzzle in the mouth, they turn away reproofs.
verses.20:30: Hidden wisdom and unseen treasure—what benefit is there in both?
verses.20:31: Better is a person who hides his folly than a person who hides his wisdom.
verses.21:1: Child, have you sinned? Do not add to it anymore, and pray concerning your former sins.
verses.21:2: As from the face of a serpent, flee from sin; for if you approach, it will bite you. Its teeth are the teeth of a lion, destroying the souls of people.
verses.21:3: All lawlessness is like a two-edged sword; for its wound there is no healing.
verses.21:4: Intimidation and insolence will lay waste to wealth; so the house of a proud person will be laid waste.
verses.21:5: The prayer of a poor person reaches from the mouth to His ears, and His judgment comes swiftly.
verses.21:6: One who hates reproof is in the footsteps of a sinner, but the one who fears the Lord will turn back in heart.
verses.21:7: The one who is mighty in tongue is known from afar, but the discerning person knows when he slips.
verses.21:8: The one who builds his house with the money of others is like one who gathers his stones for winter.
verses.21:9: Tow gathered together is a gathering of lawless ones, and their end is a flame of fire.
verses.21:10: The way of sinners is made smooth with stones, yet at its end is the pit of Hades.
verses.21:11: The one who keeps the law masters his thinking, and the completion of the fear of the Lord is wisdom.
verses.21:12: One who is not shrewd will not be instructed; there is a shrewdness that multiplies bitterness.
verses.21:13: The knowledge of a wise person will increase like a flood, and his counsel is like a spring of life.
verses.21:14: The inward parts of a fool are like a shattered vessel, and he will not hold any knowledge.
verses.21:15: If a knowledgeable person hears a wise word, he will praise it and add to it; the self-indulgent person heard it and it displeased him, and he cast it behind his back.
verses.21:16: The discourse of a fool is like a burden on a journey, but grace will be found on the lip of an understanding person.
verses.21:17: The mouth of a prudent person will be sought in the assembly, and one will ponder his words in the heart.
verses.21:18: Like a ruined house, so is wisdom to a fool, and the knowledge of one lacking understanding is unexamined words.
verses.21:19: Discipline is fetters on senseless feet, and like shackles on the right hand.
verses.21:20: A fool raises his voice high in laughter, but a shrewd man will scarcely smile quietly.
verses.21:21: Like a golden ornament to a prudent person is discipline, and like a bracelet on the right arm.
verses.21:22: The foot of a fool is quick into a house, but a well-experienced person will show modesty before another's face.
verses.21:23: A senseless person peers from the door into a house, but a disciplined man will stand outside.
verses.21:24: It is lack of discipline for a person to listen by the door, but the prudent person will be weighed down with dishonor.
verses.21:25: The lips of strangers will be weighed down in these things, but the words of the prudent will be weighed on a scale.
verses.21:26: In the mouth of fools is their heart, but the heart of the wise is their mouth.
verses.21:27: When an ungodly person curses Satan, he himself curses his own soul.
verses.21:28: A whisperer defiles his own soul, and he will be hated in the neighborhood.
verses.22:1: A lazy man is compared to a filthy stone, and everyone will hiss at his dishonor.
verses.22:2: A lazy man is compared to a lump of dung; everyone who picks him up will shake off his hand.
verses.22:3: A father's shame is in the birth of an undisciplined son, and a daughter is born to loss.
verses.22:4: A prudent daughter will inherit her husband, and she who brings shame is a grief to the one who fathered her.
verses.22:5: An insolent woman shames father and husband, and she will be dishonored by both.
verses.22:6: Untimely talk is music in mourning, but whips and discipline belong to wisdom at every time.
verses.22:9: The one who teaches a fool is gluing together a potsherd, waking a sleeper from a deep sleep.
verses.22:10: The one who talks to a fool is talking to someone dozing off, and at the end he will say, "What is it?"
verses.22:11: Weep over a dead man, for he lacks light; and weep over a fool, for he lacks understanding. Weep more gently over a dead man, because he has found rest; but the life of the fool is worse than death.
verses.22:12: Mourning for a dead man is seven days, but for a fool and an ungodly man, all the days of his life.
verses.22:13: Do not multiply words with a foolish man, and do not go to one without understanding. Be on guard against him, so that you do not have trouble and will by no means be defiled by his spattering. Turn aside from him and you will find rest, and you will by no means grow weary at his madness.
verses.22:14: What is heavier than lead? And what is its name except a fool?
verses.22:15: Sand and salt and a lump of iron are easier to bear than a person without understanding.
verses.22:16: A wooden tie-beam bound into a building will not come apart in an earthquake; so a heart established upon a thought of counsel will not become timid at the time.
verses.22:17: A heart settled upon a mind of understanding is like a sand-plaster ornament on a smooth wall.
verses.22:18: Stakes set on a high place will by no means stand firm against the wind; so a timid heart upon a foolish thought will by no means stand firm against any fear.
verses.22:19: The one who pricks an eye will bring down tears, and one who pricks a heart reveals feeling.
verses.22:20: One who throws a stone at birds scares them away, and the one who reproaches a friend will dissolve friendship.
verses.22:21: If you draw a sword against a friend, do not despair, for there is a way back.
verses.22:22: If you open your mouth against a friend, do not be afraid, for there is reconciliation, except for reproach and arrogance and the revealing of a secret and a treacherous blow; at these things every friend will flee away.
verses.22:23: Gain trust with your neighbor in poverty, so that you may be filled together in his good things; stay with him in a time of affliction, so that you may be a co-heir in his inheritance.
verses.22:24: Before fire come the vapor of a furnace and smoke; so before bloodshed come insults.
verses.22:25: I will not be ashamed to shelter a friend, and I will by no means hide from his face,
verses.22:26: and if evil things happen to me because of him, everyone who hears will be on guard against him.
verses.22:27: Who will give me a guard over my mouth and a shrewd seal upon my lips, so that I may not fall from it and my tongue destroy me?
verses.23:1: Lord, Father and Master of my life, do not abandon me to their counsel; do not let me fall by them.
verses.23:2: Who will set whips over my thought and the discipline of wisdom over my heart, so that they may not spare my errors of ignorance, and it will by no means pass over their sins,
verses.23:3: so that my errors of ignorance may not multiply and my sins increase, and I fall before the adversaries, and my enemy gloat over me?
verses.23:4: Lord, Father and God of my life, do not give me haughtiness of eyes,
verses.23:5: and turn desire away from me.
verses.23:6: Do not let appetite of the belly and lust overtake me, and do not give me over to a shameless soul.
verses.23:7: Discipline of the mouth. Listen to the discipline of the mouth, children, and the one who keeps it will by no means be caught; in his lips
verses.23:8: a sinner and a reviler and an arrogant person will be left behind; they will stumble by them.
verses.23:9: Do not accustom your mouth to an oath, and do not become accustomed to the naming of the Holy One.
verses.23:10: For just as a household servant who is examined constantly will not lack a bruise, so also the one who swears and utters the name continually will by no means be cleansed from sin.
verses.23:11: A man of many oaths will be filled with lawlessness, and a whip will not depart from his house. If he offends, his sin is upon him, and if he disregards it, he has sinned doubly; and if he has sworn in vain, he will not be justified, for his house will be filled with calamities.
verses.23:12: There is speech matched with death; may it not be found in the inheritance of Jacob. For all these things will depart from the godly, and they will not wallow in sins.
verses.23:13: Do not accustom your mouth to foul crudeness, for there is a word of sin in it.
verses.23:14: Remember your father and mother, for you sit in council among great men, so that you may never forget yourself before them and become foolish by your habit, and wish that you had not been born, nor curse the day of your birth.
verses.23:15: A man accustomed to words of reproach will by no means be disciplined in all his days.
verses.23:16: Two kinds multiply sins, and the third will bring on wrath: a hot soul, like a burning fire, will by no means be quenched until it is consumed; a sexually immoral man in the body of his flesh will by no means stop until he kindles a fire.
verses.23:17: To a sexually immoral man all bread is sweet; he will by no means rest until he dies.
verses.23:18: A man who strays from his bed, saying in his soul, "Who sees me? Darkness is all around me, and the walls cover me, and no one sees me; why should I be afraid? The Most High will by no means remember my sins."
verses.23:19: And the eyes of people are his fear, and he does not know that the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, looking upon all the ways of people and looking closely into hidden places.
verses.23:20: Before they were created, all things were known to Him, and so also after their completion.
verses.23:21: This man will be punished in the streets of the city, and where he did not suspect, he will be seized.
verses.23:22: So also is a woman who leaves her husband and presents an heir by another man.
verses.23:23: For first, she disobeyed the law of the Most High, and second, she offended against her own husband, and third, she committed adultery in sexual immorality; she presented children by another man.
verses.23:24: This woman will be brought out into the assembly, and there will be a reckoning upon her children.
verses.23:25: Her children will not spread into a root, and her branches will not yield fruit.
verses.23:26: She will leave her memory for a curse, and her reproach will not be blotted out.
verses.23:27: And those who are left behind will recognize that nothing is better than the fear of the Lord, and nothing is sweeter than heeding the commandments of the Lord.
verses.24:1: Praise of Wisdom. Wisdom will praise her own soul, and in the midst of her people she will boast.
verses.24:2: In the assembly of the Most High she will open her mouth, and before His host she will boast:
verses.24:3: "I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, and like a mist I covered the earth.
verses.24:4: I made my dwelling in the heights, and my throne was in a pillar of cloud.
verses.24:5: I alone went around the circuit of heaven, and in the depth of the abysses I walked.
verses.24:6: In the waves of the sea and in all the earth, and among every people and nation I gained possession.
verses.24:7: Among all these I sought a resting place, and in whose inheritance will I lodge?
verses.24:8: Then the Creator of all things commanded me, and He who created me caused my tent to rest and said, 'Make your dwelling in Jacob, and receive your inheritance in Israel.'
verses.24:9: Before the age, from the beginning, He created me, and forever I will never cease.
verses.24:10: In the holy tent I ministered before Him, and so in Zion I was established.
verses.24:11: In the beloved city He likewise caused me to rest, and in Jerusalem is my authority.
verses.24:12: And I took root among an honored people, in the portion of the Lord, His inheritance.
verses.24:13: Like a cedar I grew tall in Lebanon, and like a cypress on the mountains of Hermon.
verses.24:14: Like a palm tree I grew tall on the shores, and like rose plants in Jericho; like a stately olive tree in a plain, and I grew tall like a plane tree.
verses.24:15: Like cinnamon and aspalathus I have given forth a scent of spices, and like choice myrrh I spread abroad a sweet fragrance, like galbanum and onycha and stacte, and like the vapor of frankincense in the tent.
verses.24:16: I, like a terebinth, stretched out my branches, and my branches are branches of glory and grace.
verses.24:17: I am like a vine that sprouted grace, and my blossoms are fruit of glory and wealth.
verses.24:19: Come to me, you who desire me, and be filled from my produce.
verses.24:20: For the remembrance of me is sweeter than honey, and my inheritance than a honeycomb.
verses.24:21: Those who eat me will still hunger, and those who drink me will still thirst.
verses.24:22: The one who obeys me will not be put to shame, and those who work in me will not sin."
verses.24:23: All these things are the book of the covenant of the Most High God, the law that Moses commanded as an inheritance for the congregations of Jacob,
verses.24:25: which overflows with wisdom like the Pishon, and like the Tigris in the days of new fruits;
verses.24:26: which runs full with understanding like the Euphrates, and like the Jordan in the days of harvest;
verses.24:27: which shows forth instruction like light, like the Gihon in the days of grape harvest.
verses.24:28: The first one did not finish knowing her, and so the last one did not trace her out.
verses.24:29: For her thought is more abundant than the sea, and her counsel than the great abyss.
verses.24:30: And I, like a canal from a river and like a water conduit, went out into an orchard.
verses.24:31: I said, "I will water my garden, and I will drench my garden bed." And look, the canal became a river for me, and my river became a sea.
verses.24:32: Still I will make instruction shine like the dawn, and I will show these things forth even far away.
verses.24:33: Still I will pour out teaching like prophecy, and I will leave it for eternal generations.
verses.24:34: See that I have not labored for myself alone, but for all who seek it out.
verses.25:1: In three things I was made beautiful, and I stood forth beautiful before the Lord and people: harmony of brothers, and friendship of neighbors, and a wife and a husband who accommodate each other.
verses.25:2: But my soul hated three kinds, and I greatly loathed their life: an arrogant poor man, and a lying rich man, an old adulterer lacking in understanding.
verses.25:3: In youth you have not gathered, and how could you find anything in your old age?
verses.25:4: How beautiful is judgment for gray hair, and for elders to know counsel!
verses.25:5: How beautiful is the wisdom of the aged, and thought and counsel for those who are honored!
verses.25:6: The crown of the aged is much experience, and their boast is the fear of the Lord.
verses.25:7: Nine thoughts I called blessed in my heart, and the tenth I will speak on my tongue: a man rejoicing over children, living and looking upon the fall of enemies.
verses.25:8: Blessed is the one who lives with an understanding wife, and he who has not slipped with his tongue, and he who has not served one unworthy of him.
verses.25:9: Blessed is he who has found prudence, and the one who speaks into the ears of those who listen.
verses.25:10: How great is the one who has found wisdom, yet there is no one above the one who fears the Lord.
verses.25:11: The fear of the Lord has surpassed everything; to whom will the one who holds fast to it be compared?
verses.25:13: Any wound, but not a wound of the heart; and any wickedness, but not the wickedness of a woman;
verses.25:14: any affliction, but not the affliction of those who hate; and any vengeance, but not the vengeance of enemies.
verses.25:15: There is no head above the head of a serpent, and there is no wrath above the wrath of an enemy.
verses.25:16: I would rather live with a lion and a dragon than dwell with a wicked woman.
verses.25:17: The wickedness of a woman alters her appearance, and darkens her face like sackcloth.
verses.25:18: Among his neighbors her husband will recline, and when he hears, he groans bitterly.
verses.25:19: Any evil is small compared to the evil of a woman; may the lot of a sinner fall upon her!
verses.25:20: A sandy climb under the feet of an elderly man, so is a talkative wife to a quiet husband.
verses.25:21: Do not fall before the beauty of a woman, and do not long for a woman.
verses.25:22: There is anger and shamelessness and great shame if a wife supports her husband.
verses.25:23: A downcast heart and a gloomy face and a wound of the heart is a wicked wife; drooping hands and feeble knees is she who will not make her husband happy.
verses.25:24: From a woman is the beginning of sin, and because of her we all die.
verses.25:25: Do not give water an outlet, nor a wicked wife authority.
verses.25:26: If she does not walk according to your hand, cut her off from your flesh.
verses.26:1: Blessed is the husband of a good wife, and the number of his days is double.
verses.26:2: A capable wife gladdens her husband, and he will complete his years in peace.
verses.26:3: A good wife is a good portion; she will be given in the portion of those who fear the Lord.
verses.26:4: Whether rich or poor, his heart is good, and at all times his face is cheerful.
verses.26:5: Of three things my heart was afraid, and at the fourth face I pleaded: slander of a city, and an assembly of a mob, and false accusation; all are more grievous than death.
verses.26:6: Pain of heart and mourning is a rival wife against another wife, and a scourge of the tongue communicating with all.
verses.26:7: A shaking ox-yoke is an evil wife; the one who takes hold of her is like the one who grasps a scorpion.
verses.26:8: Great anger is a drunken woman, and she will not cover up her shame.
verses.26:9: The sexual immorality of a woman is in the lifting up of the eyes, and it will be known by her eyelids.
verses.26:10: Over a daughter, unswervingly keep a firm watch, so that, finding liberty, she may not indulge herself.
verses.26:11: Keep watch after a shameless eye, and do not be surprised if she does wrong against you.
verses.26:12: As a thirsty traveler opens his mouth and will drink from any water nearby, opposite every peg she will sit, and before an arrow she will open her quiver.
verses.26:13: The grace of a wife will delight her husband, and her skill will fatten his bones.
verses.26:14: A gift of the Lord is a silent wife, and there is no equivalent for a disciplined soul.
verses.26:15: Grace upon grace is a modest wife, and no weight at all is worthy of a self-controlled soul.
verses.26:16: Like the sun rising in the heights of the Lord, so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of his house.
verses.26:17: Like a lamp shining out upon a holy lampstand, so is the beauty of a face upon a stately stature.
verses.26:18: Like golden pillars upon a silver base, so are beautiful feet upon the breast of a steadfast woman.
verses.26:28: Over two things my heart has been grieved, and at the third, wrath came upon me: a warrior suffering lack because of poverty, and men of understanding if they are treated as refuse; one who turns back from righteousness to sin—the Lord will prepare him for the sword.
verses.26:29: Hardly will a merchant keep himself free from wrongdoing, and a shopkeeper will not be acquitted of sin.
verses.27:1: For the sake of a trifling thing many have sinned, and the one who seeks to increase will turn away his eye.
verses.27:2: Between the joints of stones a peg will be fixed fast, and between selling and buying sin will be squeezed in.
verses.27:3: Unless he holds fast with diligence in the fear of the Lord, his house will quickly be overthrown.
verses.27:4: In the shaking of a sieve the rubbish remains; so does a man's refuse in his reasoning.
verses.27:5: A furnace tests a potter's vessels, and the test of a man is in his discussion.
verses.27:6: The fruit of a tree reveals its cultivation; so does the speech of the thought of a man's heart.
verses.27:7: Do not praise a man before his reasoning, for this is the test of people.
verses.27:8: If you pursue justice, you will overtake it, and you will put it on like a long robe of glory.
verses.27:9: Birds will roost with their own kind, and truth will return to those who practice it.
verses.27:10: A lion lies in wait for prey; so do sins for those who practice injustice.
verses.27:11: The discourse of a godly man is always wisdom, but the foolish man changes like the moon.
verses.27:12: In the company of those without understanding, watch the time, but in the company of a thoughtful man, stay continually.
verses.27:13: The discourse of fools is an offense, and their laughter is in the wantonness of sin.
verses.27:14: The talk of one who swears many oaths will make hair stand on end, and their strife is a stopping of the ears.
verses.27:15: The strife of the proud is a shedding of blood, and their mutual reviling is a grievous thing to hear.
verses.27:16: The one who reveals secrets has destroyed trust, and he will never find a friend after his own soul.
verses.27:17: Love a friend and keep faith with him; but if you reveal his secrets, never pursue after him.
verses.27:18: For just as a man has destroyed his enemy, so you have destroyed the friendship of your neighbor.
